title: not even a chance to sign up, RIDICULOUS!
body: I download the app hoping i can easily amd relaxingly do my to do lists. first of all i find it a little odd that i need to make an account to make to-do lists but ok understandable if i want it on other devices so i do sign up and its literally been the most frustrating 10min of my life ive experienced trying to do something simple. i go put my email address with no problem and then have to create a code. no problem, so i do. 1 code “not strong enough” so i make another and another and another more intricate with each unaccepted try. FINALLY it gets me to where i need to verify my email wich i find ridiculous just to do lists. the email never gets sent. so i try another email account of mine to see if ill even be able to get the email. i put in the code that had worked before amd guess what? “not strong enough” even though it worked before??? so i make another and another each time getting the same notice. so i devide to put in random letters big and small, numbers, signs. guess what? “not strong enough” i find this absolutely ridiculous for a simple app to do todo lists. an app like any other with nothing even remotely more special then every app on the app store, it would be the most basic app with no special features and i am 99% sure i would get adds or need to pay for the most basic functuonalities ever. but im not mad about that, nono. im mad at the fact that someone out there thought this app would be important enough to not only need an account with a password and verified email, but that it needs a password this intricate to only need to be able to work an app like amy other if not worse. im not trying to find the code to access the epstein files im just trying to make a todo list. absolutely ridiculous!

title: Gut, aber
body:
Einige Dinge sind einfach nicht gut gemacht.
1. Sich wiederholende Termine muss man mit Text machen. Das klappt nicht immer. 
2. Bei sich wiederholenden Terminen kann man nur eine Anfangszeit, jedoch keine Zeitdauer eingeben.
3. Bei sich wiederholenden Terminen werden in Zukunft nicht alle Termine angezeigt, sondern nur immer der nächste.

Eigentlich wäre die App genial, aber zumindest der zweite und dritte Punkt schränken die Benutzerfreundlichkeit und die Anwendung was die Planung angeht stark ein.

Vielleicht wollen die Herausgeber cool und modern sein anstatt, die Anwendung viel einfacher zu machen. Eine Möglichkeit wäre z. B. Die Texteingabe zu behalten und es aber auch wie in Kalenderfunktion anzubieten. Somit hätte man das Problem der Zeitspanne auch gelöst. 

Gut ist die Möglichkeit zur Zusammenarbeit und dass es Geräte- und Systemübergreifend ist.

title: Ist really a bit over the top
body:
As someone who loved Wunderlist, i was delighted to know my office opted to use todoist since it was so close to Wunderlist. After using it now for a while, i always struggle to understand where to find what i need to check on the status of an issue or a todo. Its a mess and not intuitive at all.. I have not the time to delve into the intricacies of todoist ( and i did not on wunderlist either ) and i dont want to.  But Wunderlist had that intuitiveness that todoist does not, so that was not an issue.

My advice : do not overwhelm users with gamification, avoid lots and lots of options and keep it simple.

Todoist is not a game, not an mmo and associated with a todo function which in itself makes people want to spend as less time as possible with . Now confront them with an overwhelming amount of settings, groups and views and you know where the experience is going. Not everyone wants to learn this. And sometimes people are forced to use it.

This is only my view. Hope it helps you working on the experience of the app.

title: Totally useless
body: One of the most overrated apps according to me. I've been using a premium account for one year now and will not renew. I really though it would help me organising my tasks, but I barely used the service as it's really useless to me, as a freelancer. Lest say I get a job which has to be done before the date X. The only way for it to appear everyday in Todoist is to enter "work on it everyday until X". That's fine so far. But: if I mark my task as finished on day X-5, this same task will reappear on day X-4, X-3, X-2, X-1 and X. And if I don't mark it as finished each time, it appears as missed deadline task. Furthermore, setting a task is meant to be easy as it uses common language, but it's not. Depending on the vocabulary used, the app will sometimes recognise elements as part of the task/deadline, sometimes not. I had to reformulate my input up to 4 or 5 times on one occasion. And last but not least: what's this Karma nonsense about?
